observed: bounded content-free model, queue, tool, liveness, and exporter attributes
diagnostic async queue drop is itself measured
request bytes, time-to-first-byte, prompt component sizes, and usage remain separate
exporter failure and health use bounded categories rather than raw errors
observer hooks report lifecycle without replacing requests, tool arguments, or execution callbacks
observer callback exceptions are fail-open and the agent loop continues
request and tool lifecycles have explicit start, end, duration, status, and correlation identity
behavior-affecting legacy hook returns are not observability requirements
malformed user-editable telemetry metadata becomes a startup warning instead of startup failure
missing event timestamps serialized as zero and downstream collectors dropped records
traces and metrics arriving did not prove log coverage
telemetry lifecycle and timestamp truth require their own negative controls

adopted: monotonic start and end captured at the actual boundary
observer errors never change product output, error, effect, or surface
writer and flush occur after the foreground product result
buffer drop and writer failure are explicit observer diagnostics
each signal and lifecycle path requires its own coverage countertest
rejected: observer data in model context or user surface
t5Counterexamples: trace field contaminates the provider request
operation throws and observer must preserve the same error identity
